channel.title: Simulator on Joulie
channel.description: Recent content in Simulator on Joulie

item.title: Simulated Cluster
item.description:
The simulated cluster runs the real Joulie components on emulated bare-metal nodes, on one machine with Docker. The agent discovers and caps emulated hardware through the same files and tools it uses on a real node, the controller manager reads node power from Prometheus, and the scheduler extender scores real pods.

Use it to see a change to the agent, the controller manager, the extender, the chart or the simulator work across components. A change to discovery or capping alone is checked faster by the hwemu tests in cmd/agent (go test ./cmd/agent/ -run Hwemu).

item.title: Workload Scenarios
item.description: A workload scenario runs a workload through the simulated cluster and checks what happened: whether the jobs completed, where they were placed, how long they took, what energy they used, and how Joulie’s settings compare with each other or with no Joulie at all. The jobs are real Kubernetes Jobs on KWOK Nodes, driven by the simulator’s v1 engine on the emulated hardware, so a cap the agent writes slows the jobs on that Node.

item.title: Installation
item.description:
This page installs the simulator into a Kubernetes cluster you already have, or runs it from a workstation. To try Joulie with nothing but Docker, use the simulated cluster instead: it creates the cluster and installs everything.

The commands use the namespace joulie-sim-demo and the release joulie-simulator, the defaults of make simulator-install.

Prerequisites

  • A Kubernetes cluster (real, or kind for local work), with kubectl pointed at it.
  • helm v3 or later.

Install with Helm

helm upgrade --install joulie-simulator oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim \
 --version <version> -n joulie-sim-demo --create-namespace

helm show values oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim --version <version> prints the values you can override; helm uninstall joulie-simulator -n joulie-sim-demo removes it. The chart models the Nodes labelled joulie.io/managed=true (SIM_NODE_SELECTOR); KWOK and Standalone Modes says how to point Joulie at it.

item.title: Emulate Mode
item.description:
Emulate mode emulates the bare-metal nodes of a cluster spec at the boundary the agent sees: the files it reads and writes, and the GPU tools it runs. An unmodified agent then runs its real discovery and capping code against each node, while Kubernetes scheduling stays real. The simulated cluster runs it; to run it yourself, see Installation. Nodes the spec does not list keep the label-based model of KWOK and standalone modes.

Turn it on with SIM_EMULATE=true and SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC; every variable is under Simulator emulate mode.

item.title: KWOK and Standalone Modes
item.description:
Outside emulate mode the simulator models each node from its labels: it keeps per-node power, cap and thermal state in memory and serves it over HTTP, with no files and no GPU tools. It runs in one of two ways:

  • KWOK mode: a Kubernetes cluster whose worker nodes are KWOK fake nodes. The real controller manager, scheduler extender and agent in pool mode run against the simulator’s HTTP API. The benchmark experiments run this way.
  • Standalone mode (SIM_STANDALONE=true): no Kubernetes. The simulator places the jobs of a trace and runs the policy baselines itself, in simulated time.

How KWOK mode works

  1. Node labels give each fake node its simulated hardware.
  2. The controller manager resolves that hardware and writes the desired profile and caps into NodeTwin.spec.
  3. The agent (pool mode) reads NodeTwin.spec and sends control intents to /control/{node}.
  4. The simulator applies them, advances power, energy and job progress, and serves telemetry on /otlp/telemetry/{node}.
  5. The next reconcile reacts to the new state; the scheduler extender scores pods from NodeTwin.status.

item.title: Workload Generation
item.description:
workloadgen (simulator/cmd/workloadgen) writes synthetic traces of AI cluster workloads for the simulator to run. Workload Simulator says how the simulator runs them.

go run ./simulator/cmd/workloadgen --out trace.jsonl --jobs 200 --seed 7

The traces hold CPU and GPU jobs, memory-bound jobs, and workloads of several pods, such as distributed training and hyperparameter searches. Network, disk and framework communication are not modelled: their cost is folded into each workload’s utilisation and bottleneck signals.

Trace format

A trace is JSON Lines. A type=workload record is one logical workload with its pods by role, for inspection only; a type=job record is one runnable pod, and the simulator runs these.

item.title: Workload Simulator
item.description:
This page says how the simulator runs a workload trace: which Kubernetes objects it creates and how caps slow each job. Workload Generation describes the traces; Power Simulator the power side of a node.

Two engines: legacy and v1

SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL selects the engine that runs a trace.

Engine Where Started by Kubernetes objects A job that cannot progress Results
legacy outside emulate mode SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH, replayed from startup one bare pod per job, deleted when done completed by force after SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_FORCE_COMPLETE (120 s) joulie_sim_job_* counters at /metrics
v1 emulate mode the run API, or SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH as an implicit run one batch/v1 Job per group, completed through KWOK’s pod-complete Stage reported as stalled, never completed OTLP JSON Lines in the run directory, plus the run API’s status

v1 without emulate mode, and legacy with it, stop the start. The variables are in Simulator workloads and scenarios. Workload Scenarios run v1 workloads on the simulated cluster and check their completion, placement, slowdown and energy.

item.title: Power Simulator
item.description:
This page says how the simulator advances a modelled node (any node outside the emulate-mode cluster spec): its controls, its physics step and its telemetry. The models and their sources are in Hardware Modeling; how jobs progress is in Workload Simulator.

The physics step

A modelled node advances only in a physics step, in simulated time, never when it is read. One step moves caps, frequency, power and temperature toward their targets with their settling lags, in substeps of at most 100 ms, and integrates energy from the instantaneous power.

item.title: Hardware Calibration
item.description:
hwcalib (simulator/cmd/hwcalib) fits the physics of a hardware profile to a sweep measured on one of your nodes, so the simulator draws what your machine draws instead of the builtin profiles’ vendor figures and placeholders. hwcalib sweep records the sweep on the node; hwcalib fit writes the result as a local profile the simulator loads from SIM_PROFILES_DIR.

Recording a sweep

A sweep holds the node at a series of setpoints and records, at every sample, the node’s readings and the setpoints it held. Each setpoint needs at least 5 samples after it settles: with a 2 s sample period, 22 s or more.

item.title: Simulator Metrics
item.description:
This page lists every metric and event the simulator emits, to write a query or a dashboard against it. There are three kinds:

Kind Where Mode
Prometheus metrics about the simulator itself (joulie_sim_*) scraped at /metrics every mode
OpenTelemetry metrics and events about the emulated nodes and the facility metrics pushed as OTLP JSON over HTTP; events in events.jsonl, pushed when a logs endpoint is set emulate mode
Compatibility exporters: the Prometheus formats of Kepler, dcgm-exporter and the ROCm device-metrics-exporter /exporters/<name>/metrics, opt-in emulate mode

The OpenTelemetry names are spelled once, in pkg/otel/semconv, and the controller manager reads the same names back from Prometheus. Their Prometheus spelling is computed by pkg/otel/promname.
